SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch Station 2/33
REPORT
Date December 20, 1933.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. ... No. D 5537）

Subject (in full) Alleged appointment of two former officers of the Berlin Police Force to posts as reorganizers of a police force in China.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by A. J. McEuen

With reference to the attached cutting from the "North China Daily News" of November 22, 1933, containing report regarding the alleged appointment of two former officers of the Berlin Police Force to posts as reorganizers of a police force in China, it is persistently rumoured that the officers concerned are Grzesinsky and Bernard Weiss and that they either have arrived in China recently or are on their way to this country.

It is reported that both Grzesinsky and B. Weiss are members of the left wing of the German Social Democratic Party and that prior to the advent of the present regime in Germany they held the posts of President and Vice-President of the Berlin Police Force respectively. Following the establishment of the Nazi regime in January 1933 they fled to Paris where they resided until recently. It is also reported that their names appear on the list of persons who have forfeited their German nationality and that a criminal charge is pending in Berlin against B. Weiss who is alleged to have been connected with gambling houses in that city.

It has been learned from a reliable local German source that the services of the above two individuals were secured for the Nanking Government by Mr. T. V. Soong during the latter's recent sojourn in Europe.

No confirmation has so far been obtained of the report that Grzesinsky or B. Weiss have already arrived in Shanghai.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
（签名）
Dec. 20 - 1933

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特科第2股，分站 2/33
报告
日期：1933年12月20日。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事与特别股登记处。档案号……编号 D 5537）

事由（全称） 据称两名前柏林警察部队官员被任命为中国某警察部队重组者。
呈报人：副督察普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev） 转呈人：A. J. McEuen

鉴于附上的1933年11月22日《字林西报》剪报，其中包含关于据称两名前柏林警察部队官员被任命为中国某警察部队重组者的报道，有持续不断的谣言称，涉事官员为格热辛斯基（Grzesinsky）和伯纳德·魏斯（Bernard Weiss），他们要么最近已抵达中国，要么正在前来本国的途中。

据报道，格热辛斯基和B.魏斯均为德国社会民主党左翼成员，在德国现政权上台之前，他们分别担任柏林警察部队的主管和副主管。在1933年1月纳粹政权建立后，他们逃往巴黎，并一直居住至最近。另有报道称，他们的名字出现在已被剥夺德国国籍的人员名单上，且柏林方面正对B.魏斯提起刑事诉讼，指控他与该市的赌场有关联。

据一位可靠的本地德国消息来源获悉，上述两人的服务是由宋子文先生在其近期旅居欧洲期间为南京政府招募的。

截至目前，尚未获得证实格热辛斯基或B.魏斯已抵达上海的报告。

A. 普罗科菲耶夫
副督察

特科主管。
（签名）
1933年12月20日

BERLIN POLICEMAN
COMING HERE
Persistent Reports That
Bernard Weiss Is
On His Way
BERLIN, Dec. 8.—The property
of Bernard Weiss, the Socialist
ex-vice president of the Berlin
police, has been confiscated. The
value was 4,000 marks.
It is persistently reported that
Weiss recently left Paris for
Shanghai following an offer to
“reorganize the Chinese police.”
It is further stated that, before
his departure, Weiss wrote to a
number of his former colleagues
in the Berlin police inviting them
to join him.—Reuter.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 7, 1933

GERMAN EX-POLICE
FOR CHINA

Berlin Reports State
Former Chiefs Will
Function Here

NOTHING IS KNOWN OF
REPORT LOCALLY

BERLIN, Dec. 6.—It is stated
in semi-official circles here that the
former Socialist police chiefs of
Berlin, Weiss and Grzesinski, have
arrived in China, having been
summoned to Shanghai "to re-
organize the Chinese police."
Before leaving Paris, Herr
Weiss is reported to have written
to a number of his former col-
laborators in the Berlin police,
and it is believed that same have
signified their willingness to join
him.—Reuter.
***Inquiries made locally yester-
day, following receipt of the cabled
information, failed to secure any
enlightenment on the message.
Officials of the Shanghai Municipal
Police stated they had no knowledge
of either the persons mentioned or
their reported mission. The Public
Safety Bureau also denied any
knowledge of the matter. It was
suggested that the two former
Berlin police officials might have
been engaged by the Cantonese
authorities.

德国前警察

柏林，12月6日电。——此处半官方人士称，前柏林社会主义警察主管魏斯和格热辛斯基（Grzesinski）已抵达中国，他们是应召前往上海“重组中国警察”的。
据报道，魏斯在离开巴黎前，曾写信给他在柏林警察部队的一些前同僚，据信这些人已表示愿意加入他。——路透社。
***昨日在收到电传信息后进行的本地查询，未能就该消息获得任何确切信息。上海公共租界工部局警务处官员表示，他们对提及的人员或其据称的任务均不知情。公安局也否认对此事有任何了解。有人推测，这两名前柏林警察官员可能是受广东当局聘用。

Subject (in full) Ex-Berlin Police officials reported to be in
Government service.

Made by and Forwarded by Superintendent Tan Shao Liang.

Enquiries made at the Public Safety Bureau
Headquarters, the Chinese Municipality and the Shanghai
Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have failed
to confirm the report that Weiss and Grzesinski have
been appointed by the Chinese Government to reorganize
the Chinese Police locally.

It has been unable to ascertain whether the
two former Berlin police officials have taken up appointments
with the Canton Government as the Canton Authorities have
no agents in Shanghai at present.

TRANSLATION FROM GERMAN OF A COMMUNICATION
ADDRESSED TO "BERNHARD WEISS," COMMISSIONER
OF POLICE, SHANGHAI.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5537
914134）

Frankfurt-on-Main,
March 8, 1934.

Commissioner of Police Bernhard Weiss,
Reorganiser of the Police Force in Shanghai,
Shanghai, China.

Sir,

By chance I have learned of your address and
permit myself to write you to make the following
requests:

In your new position in Shanghai as 'Reorganiser
of the Chinese Police' you need a few men to assist
you, and I offer you my services being a man of
considerable experience.

Due to the strict censorship now prevalent in
Germany I am unable to give you full details con-
cerning myself.

I am married, have no children and am thirty
years of age; the other men are also of the same
age. Upon receipt of a favourable reply from
yourself we will leave immediately.

At present we are almost destitute and are being
assisted by benevolent societies, in consequence of
which we are unable to raise the necessary funds
for the journey from here to Shanghai. It would
therefore facilitate matters if you would send us
some money for Passports, visas, passages, travelling-
expenses and a small amount to allow us to keep our
families in Germany for the first three months.

I have been to the Central Europe Travel Bureau
where enquiries elicit the following information:-
Passage from Frankfurt-on-Main to Shanghai....RM. 752;
Passport and Visa......RM. 100. In addition to
provide our families with the necessities of live for
a period of three or four months would cost about
RM. 300 per family. Thus in all each man would
need approximately RM. 1200. Arrangements could be
made later regarding the transport, etc. of our
families. The above mentioned sums could be deduct-
ed little by little, from our salaries after reaching
China.

Trusting that you will give this letter the
consideration that it deserves and assuring you that
upon receipt of a favourable answer we would be
prepared to leave immediately,

Yours respectfully,

致“伯恩哈德·魏斯”，上海警察总监的一封信的德文译文。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别股登记处。
编号 D 5537
914134）

美因河畔法兰克福，
1934年3月8日。

警察总监伯恩哈德·魏斯先生，
上海警察部队重组者，
中国上海。

先生，

我偶然得知了您的地址，
冒昧致信向您提出以下请求：

您在上海担任“中国警察重组者”的新职位上，需要一些人协助您，我作为一名拥有丰富经验的人，愿为您提供服务。

由于德国目前实行严格的审查制度，我无法向您提供关于我本人的全部细节。

我已婚，无子女，年龄三十岁；其他几人也是同龄。一旦收到您的肯定回复，我们将立即启程。

目前我们几乎身无分文，正依靠慈善团体的援助，因此我们无法筹集从此地前往上海所需的旅费。如果您能寄给我们一些用于办理护照、签证、船票、旅途开销的钱款，以及一小笔让我们家属在德国维持前三个月生活的费用，事情将会容易得多。

我曾前往中欧旅行社咨询，获得如下信息：
从美因河畔法兰克福到上海的船票……752帝国马克；
护照和签证……100帝国马克。此外，
为家属提供三到四个月的生活必需品，每户家庭大约需要300帝国马克。因此，每人总共大约需要1200帝国马克。关于我们家属的运输等事宜，可以稍后安排。上述款项可以在我们抵达中国后，从我们的薪水中间接扣除。

相信您会给予这封信应有的考虑，并向您保证，一旦收到肯定的答复，我们将准备立即启程，

此致
敬礼，
